metadata.name: two-person-approval
metadata.description: Two of three named people must approve before the write lands, and A REJECTION ARRIVING BEFORE THE SECOND APPROVAL VETOES IT: `onBranchError: "fail"` is read before `k` ever matters, so one rejection fails the whole run — once the remaining gates are answered — whatever the other two would have said. The VERDICT is settled by that rejection; the run itself stays `awaiting_gate` until the other people vote, so a single rejection and silence leaves it parked, not failed. Arriving after the second approval it still fails the run, but the write has already landed — see `labels.residue-late-veto`. Copy this file for two-of-three-with-a-veto; it is NOT k-of-n tolerance of a dissenter. There is no `approval.mode: quorum` — k-of-n is N gates and a quorum join, which is why the field was deleted.

labels.residue: a short-circuiting quorum join leaves the unneeded gate OPEN — JoinNode's documented straggler-cancellation gap
labels.residue-veto: ONE rejection fails the run, so `k: 2` buys no tolerance for a dissenter: it only short-circuits the wait for the third person. `onBranchError: "skip"` WOULD ALSO REFUSE a run that did not reach `k` — since §A.75 the fold enforces `k` as a floor whatever `onBranchError` says, so ONE approval out of three is refused AT THE BARRIER (`E_QUORUM_UNREACHABLE`) rather than landing the write, which is what it used to do. The two values now differ only in WHEN: `fail` refuses at the first rejection, `skip` at the barrier once every gate has been answered. This example ships `fail` until a maintainer picks between them; the measured table for both is in `packages/core/test/graph/two-person-approval.test.ts`.
labels.residue-late-veto: THE VETO IS NOT UNCONDITIONAL, because the gate the short-circuit left open is still answerable. Measured: alice approve, bob approve, carol REJECT ends `status=failed` with the write ALREADY LANDED — the barrier released on two approvals, `save` ran, and carol's rejection then failed a run whose effect had happened. Two approvals are the point of no return; a third person who intends to veto must do it before the second approval.
